reason: The contract (problem.txt) explicitly requires that when several experts share the largest logit, the LOWEST expert index wins, and states ties are routine because logits are in reduced precision. The kernel's scan uses `take = v >= best` (kernel.py line 17), so an equal later value overwrites the incumbent, yielding the highest tied index. Probe t6 confirmed this at runtime: with explicit fp16 ties the kernel returned [2,3,3,2] where the contract requires [1,0,3,0] (wrong on all three tied rows); on 4096x8 coarsely quantized fp16 logits, 1174 rows contained ties and the kernel mismatched the lowest-index rule on all 1174 (100%) while mismatching the highest-index rule on 0. Selected values always equaled the row max (0 wrong), so the max is computed correctly but the tie-break is exactly inverted — a direct violation of a behaviour the contract requires, on inputs the contract explicitly declares normal.
